messages.subject: geom_point(shape=...) bug
parts:
It seems that when you specify a non-default shape in geom_point, it
still plots the default filled-circle shape (16) and then the
requested shape:

#try with shape 4, which is supposed to be an X
qplot(1:10,1:10)+geom_point(shape=I(4))

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: geom_point(shape=...) bug
parts:
Hi Mike,

Yes, that's because qplot adds a points layer by default. You want
one of the following:

qplot(1:10,1:10, shape=I(4))
qplot(1:10, 1:10, geom="blank") + geom_point(shape=4)

Hadley

messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Re: geom_point(shape=...) bug
parts:
Hi Mike -

It's the commands that you're using.  With the qplot() command you're creating the plot with the dots, then you are adding a layer with the X's above it.  I think either of the following commands is what you want :

df <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 1:10)
ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y), data = df) +
  geom_point(shape = I(4))

or

qplot(x, y, data = df, geom = 'point', shape = I(4))

Cheers
david.
